clue.text: They teach five elements in order to develop wanderlust

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to begin feeling restless and eager to travel

indicators.note: the elements (letters) of the preceding words are put into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A school's teachers instruct pupils in five topics so that they will come to love travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements in order' says the letters of THEY TEACH FIVE are rearranged; all thirteen are used. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and longing to roam is said, idiomatically, to be impatient to move on, with feet that won't keep still.

clue.text: Desperately hope, with bad clothing, to sleep around

indicators.note: done desperately, the letters are thrown about wildly, an anagram signal
the clothing of a word is its outside, so its first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone longs, while badly dressed, to be promiscuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' takes the first and last letters of 'bad', B and D; 'Desperately' rearranges them with HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go from one partner's bed to another's is informal slang for being promiscuous.

clue.text: Select a flower, say, with relish

indicators.note: 'say' asks for the phrase to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: select means pick; a flower is a lily, giving 'pick a lily'

explanation.surface: Choose a bloom and enjoy it with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'pick a lily' matches the name of the mustard pickle; 'with' is a link word, and 'relish' is the condiment, not enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is a chopped vegetable pickle in mustard sauce, a type of condiment served with cold meats.

clue.text: Bet loads, chiefly in poker?

indicators.note: 'in' places those letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: poker is a card game

indicators.note: chiefly means the head letters of the words before it are used

explanation.surface: Wager heavily, mostly at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chiefly' gives B and L, the first letters of 'Bet loads', set 'in' GAME (poker). Read whole, staking a lot at poker is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Staking a lot of money on cards is a risky wager, the very thing a punter does.

clue.text: Skinny Albert oddly not one thrown down in challenge

parts.note: skinny means thin and bony, gaunt

indicators.note: not the odd letters, so the even-placed letters of the name are kept

explanation.surface: A thin man named Albert, strangely, isn't the one hurled to the floor in a dare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly not' drops the odd letters of ALBERT (A, B, R), keeping L, E, T. To throw down the glove was the old way of issuing a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight threw down his armoured glove to challenge an opponent to combat.

clue.text: Part of ladder where cats possibly climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: cats are an example of household pets

explanation.surface: A ladder rung where cats might be scrambling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns PETS upwards in this down clue. 'where' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung of a ladder is also called a tread, a foothold you climb on.

clue.text: Shockingly, bare necessity is on the rise in the city

indicators.note: shockingly suggests a jolt that jumbles the letters
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a necessity is a need

explanation.surface: Disturbingly, basic want is growing in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shockingly' rearranges BARE to ABER; 'on the rise' turns NEED upwards to DEEN. 'is' is a link. ABERDEEN is a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, the granite port on the North Sea.

clue.text: Gee, are we glad to be back in Alabama?

definitions.text: Gee, are we glad to be back in Alabama?

parts.words: Gee, are we glad to be back in Alabama?
parts.note: a sigh of relief at returning to one's own house, nodding to the song title about Alabama

explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes the song 'Sweet Home Alabama'; the answer is the old saying sewn on samplers, the relief of being back where you live.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase expresses joy at returning to the place one lives, the comfort of one's own house.

clue.text: Articles about organised crime, baseball and apple pie?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the next part

parts.note: the articles A, AN and A

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper features on the Mafia and on national icons of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges CRIME to MERIC, which the articles A and AN, A go 'about'. 'Organised crime' wants to be the Mafia; it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Things typical of the United States, like its national game and favourite dessert, are collectively called this.

clue.text: Thanks. I don't like this. It's unthinkable

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
boo is a cry of disapproval

explanation.surface: A grudging thank-you followed by a complaint about something too awful to consider.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is something prohibited by custom, too forbidden even to contemplate.

clue.text: And here, from Cicero, is some morality

parts.note: et is Latin for and
hic is Latin for here

explanation.surface: A Roman orator offers a moral lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Cicero' says the words are to be put into Latin, Cicero being the Roman orator; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle, one part of a code of conduct.

clue.text: See 18 Down
Spontaneity from this compiler is a sign of life!

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I'm
a pulse shows that someone is alive

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that being spontaneous proves he is alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this compiler' is the setter himself, so 'this compiler is' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse means acting suddenly, without forethought, which is what spontaneity is.

clue.text: See 1
Announced education cuts

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: lessons are what education is given in

explanation.surface: A government declares budget cuts to schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' turns LESSONS (schooling) into its sound-alike, a verb meaning reduces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce or diminish something is to make it smaller, a synonym of cuts as a verb.

clue.text: Wet feathers at the end of a space mission

parts.note: to splash is to wet
down is fine soft feathers

explanation.surface: Damp plumage after a voyage into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsules returning from orbit landed in the ocean, so the landing at sea ended the flight.

clue.text: See 8
Obsessive follower of the start of crisis in Suez?

indicators.note: follower of puts the first piece after the second
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy

explanation.surface: A fanatic devoted to the beginnings of the Suez crisis of 1956.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obsessive follower' looks like a fan; it is ANAL coming after C, 'the start of crisis'. 'in' is a link; Suez is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez is a famous artificial waterway linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea.

clue.text: Emperor whose refusal to admit a European gets a role in contention when picked

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the next pieces go inside

parts.note: non is the French refusal, no
a Pole is a European from Poland

indicators.note: 'in' puts the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: a bone of contention is something to pick a fight over, so 'a bone to pick'
a role is a part

explanation.surface: An emperor who refused a foreigner entry gets a disputed part when chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: NON (French 'no') admits A POLE, giving the first name; A PART goes 'in' BONE, from 'bone of contention' and 'a bone to pick'. 'whose' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corsican general crowned himself ruler of the French in 1804.

clue.text: For the audience, modicum of humour?

indicators.note: for listeners, so the word is as heard rather than written

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, a modicum

explanation.surface: A comedian offering the crowd just a little comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the audience' says a word for a tiny amount, WHIT, is heard as a word for cleverness in jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit is the quick, clever use of words to amuse, a kind of comedy.

clue.text: Transporter's attempt to interrupt composer

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Richard Wagner was a German composer
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A carrier tries to cut short a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transporter' suggests a machine, but here it is an old-fashioned carter; the 's is short for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner drives a horse-drawn wagon, carrying goods from place to place.

clue.text: Jump and dive without peeing to begin with

indicators.note: without means losing the letter that follows

parts.note: to dive is to plunge

indicators.note: to begin with means the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Leap and plunge in without first relieving yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUNGE (dive) 'without' P, the first letter of 'peeing', leaves the answer; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, a spring or leap at something.

clue.text: Payback before first half of the game? That's barking!

indicators.note: before places this piece ahead of the next

parts.note: 'pay' turned back reads the other way round
the game is ping-pong, whose first half is ping

explanation.surface: Revenge before half-time? That's mad!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Payback' splits as PAY turned back. 'barking' looks like British slang for mad; it is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dog making shrill, sharp noises is doing exactly what barking describes.

clue.text: Second coffee?

explanation.surface: A moment for a quick cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a moment of time; coffee from granules dissolved in water is a quick kind.

clue.text: Failed blind date leaving lad broke

indicators.note: failed means gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A doomed romantic set-up left the young man without money.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of BLIND DATE make the answer plus LAD, which is 'leaving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing money to others is the state of someone without funds.

clue.text: Start filming type of movie

explanation.surface: A director calls for cameras to roll on a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A director shouts this word to begin a take; it also names a genre of fights and car chases.

clue.text: Lie with a meal, eating somehow heals

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: food is a meal

indicators.note: somehow means arranged in some way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lying down with dinner, which somehow cures you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles the word for curing, and 'eating' puts that scramble inside the word for a meal. 'with a' is a link; 'Lie' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untrue statement made to deceive.

clue.text: See 1
Fenced enclosure protects this garden

indicators.note: the words protect, enclosing within them, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A fenced pen guarding a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in 'fencED ENclosure'; 'this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the Biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Dump part of London lacking waterfront

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a stretch is removed

parts.note: Shoreditch is a district in East London
the shore is the land at the water's edge

explanation.surface: An area of London without a riverside is a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOREDITCH is a district of East London; take away SHORE. 'Dump' is a verb meaning discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to abandon or get rid of it, informally.

clue.text: See 8
Bring back memories of the night before, cuddling Roger

indicators.note: cuddling means holding inside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: eve is the evening before a day
Roger is radio language for 'understood', OK

explanation.surface: Reminiscing about last night, hugging a man called Roger.
explanation.walkthrough: EVE 'cuddling' OK; 'Roger' is radio speak for 'message received'.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to call it to mind.

clue.text: Space for tricky bowler spinning low

indicators.note: tricky suggests something devious, so the letters are worked into a new order
spinning means turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as a cow does

explanation.surface: Room for a crafty cricket bowler whose spinning delivery stays low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges BOWLER to ELBOWR; 'spinning' turns MOO (low, as cattle) into OOM. 'for' is a link; the cricket surface is a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move freely.
